```{r customLeaflet, echo=FALSE}
# adapted from `plotLeaflet` -- drops clustering

plotLeaflet_nocluster <- function(object){
  explorerURL <- "http://apps.neotomadb.org/explorer/"
  df1 <- as.data.frame(object)
  map1 <- leaflet(df1) %>%
    addTiles(urlTemplate = 'http://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png') %>%
    addCircleMarkers(lng = df1$long,
                     lat = df1$lat,
                     popup = paste0("<b>", df1$sitename,
                                    "</b><br><b>Description:</b> ",
                                    df1$description,
                                    "<br><a href=", 
                                    explorerURL, "?siteids=",
                                    df1$siteid,
                                    ">Explorer Link</a>"),
                    options = markerOptions(riseOnHover = TRUE))
  return(map1)
}

```


#### North American Diatoms {.tabset}
We'll start by querying the database for sites with diatom surface samples in North America.

Here, we use the `datasettype` parameter allows us to search for those specific sites. We'll include a generic leaflet plot to see the general distribution of those sites.
If you need the full list of available dataset types, run `neotoma2::get_table('datasettypes')`. (See "Dataset Types" section of "A Simple Workflow" for more information.)

To restrict the geography of our selection, we restrict our query with the `loc` parameter, and pull in an `sf` object of North America.

#### Water Chemistry data availability {.tabset}
Now, we want to see which sites with diatom data also have water chemistry data available. First, we'll query the database for sites with water chemistry data. Next, we'll compare it to sites with diatom data.

##### Code: download data
```{r waterChemAvailability_downloadData, eval=FALSE}
# water chemistry data
waterChem_NA_sites <- neotoma2::get_sites(loc = northAmerica_sf,
                                          datasettype = "water chemistry",
                                          all_data = TRUE)
plotLeaflet(waterChem_NA_sites)
saveRDS(waterChem_NA_sites,file = paste0(local_fp,"Neotoma_Local/waterChem_NorthAmerica.rds",sep = ""))

```

#### Comparing Sites for Water Chemistry and Diatoms {.tabset}
Now we'll match our site data for water chemistry against the diatom surface samples dataset, and the general diatom data. First, we'll transform each sites object into a dataframe, and add a new field to indicate which datasets each has.

##### Code
```{r waterchem_vs_diatomSS, eval=FALSE}
diatom_NA_sites_df <- as.data.frame(diatom_NA_sites) %>%
  mutate(diatomGen = TRUE)
diatSS_NA_sites_df <- as.data.frame(diatSS_NA_sites) %>%
  mutate(diatomSS = TRUE)
waterchem_df <- as.data.frame(waterChem_NA_sites) %>%
  mutate(waterchem = TRUE)

# diatom surface samples and water chem join
diatSS_waterchem <- merge(diatSS_NA_sites_df,waterchem_df,
                          by = c("siteid",
                                 "sitename",
                                 "lat",
                                 "long",
                                 "area",
                                 "notes",
                                "description",
                                 "elev"),
                          all.x = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(waterchem = ifelse(is.na(waterchem), FALSE,waterchem))

# diatom general samples and water chem join
diatomGen_waterchem <- merge(diatom_NA_sites_df,waterchem_df,
                          by = c("siteid",
                                 "sitename",
                                 "lat",
                                 "long",
                                 "area",
                                 "notes",
                                "description",
                                 "elev"),
                          all.x = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(waterchem = ifelse(is.na(waterchem), FALSE,waterchem))

# map for diatom surface samples and water chemistry
# set up red/blue color palette
pal <- leaflet::colorFactor(c("red", "blue"),
                            domain = unique(diatSS_waterchem$waterchem))

map1 <- leaflet(diatSS_waterchem) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(lng = diatSS_waterchem$long,
                   lat = diatSS_waterchem$lat,
                   color = pal(diatSS_waterchem$waterchem),
                   popup = paste0("<b>", diatSS_waterchem$sitename,
                                  "</b><br><b>Description:</b> ",
                                  diatSS_waterchem$description,
                                  "<br><a href=", 
                                  explorerURL, "?siteids=",
                                  diatSS_waterchem$siteid,
                                  ">Explorer Link</a>",
                                  "<br> Water Chemistry Data:",
                                  diatSS_waterchem$waterchem,
                                  "<br> Diatom Surface Sample Data:",
                                  diatSS_waterchem$diatomSS),
                   options = markerOptions(riseOnHover = TRUE))

map1

# map for diatom general samples and water chemistry
# set up red/blue color palette
pal <- leaflet::colorFactor(c("red", "blue"),
                            domain = unique(diatomGen_waterchem$waterchem))

map2 <- leaflet(diatomGen_waterchem) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(lng = diatomGen_waterchem$long,
                   lat = diatomGen_waterchem$lat,
                   color = pal(diatomGen_waterchem$waterchem),
                   popup = paste0("<b>", diatomGen_waterchem$sitename,
                                  "</b><br><b>Description:</b> ",
                                  diatomGen_waterchem$description,
                                  "<br><a href=", 
                                  explorerURL, "?siteids=",
                                  diatomGen_waterchem$siteid,
                                  ">Explorer Link</a>",
                                  "<br> Water Chemistry Data:",
                                  diatomGen_waterchem$waterchem,
                                  "<br> Diatom General Sample Data:",
                                  diatomGen_waterchem$diatomGen),
                   options = markerOptions(riseOnHover = TRUE))

map2

```

### Using Aggregate Datasets: Loading data {.tabset}
In some instances, the collection of datasets you may want to use may not align neatly with specific sites. For example, if a project spans multiple sites, but other sampling has occurred at some of those sites, not every dataset at each of those sites is necessarily relevant to your work.

To handle this in our own work at the Academy, we have collated specific aggregate datasets -- generally, sets of diatom and associated water chemistry data. These site and dataset IDs are stored in excel spreadsheets. Here, we will walk through how to extract these IDs from excel and use them to load data from Neotoma.

In this example, we'll use dataset IDs identified for an aggregate dataset for all of North America, and set up some dataframes for further analysis.

#### Code: download data
```{r load_AD_downloadData, eval = FALSE}
sheet_name <- "North America"
xl_fp <- paste0(local_fp, "Neotoma_Local/Aggregate Datasets - Diatoms - Neotoma - 6 Jan2024.xlsx")
aggData_df <- read_xlsx(xl_fp, sheet = sheet_name) %>%
  select(`Neotoma Site ID`,
         `Site name`,
         `Neotoma Water Chemistry Dataset ID`,
         `Neotoma Diatom Dataset Id`,
         `Aggregate dataset label`,
         `Aggregate dataset name`)

## pull site IDs, use that in combination with dataset IDs
aggData_siteIDs <- aggData_df %>% 
  drop_na(`Neotoma Site ID`) %>%
  select(`Neotoma Site ID`) %>%
  as.list()

aggData_siteIDs <- unique(na.omit(aggData_df$`Neotoma Site ID`))

aggData_waterChem_sites <- get_sites(aggData_siteIDs, 
                                     datasettype = "water chemistry",
                                     all_data = TRUE)

aggData_waterChem_datasets <- get_datasets(aggData_waterChem_sites)

aggData_waterChem_dl <- get_downloads(aggData_waterChem_datasets,
                                       datasetid %in% aggData_df$`Neotoma Water Chemistry Dataset ID`,
                                      datasettype = "water chemistry")

# edit? or let run for so long?
aggData_diatom_dl <- get_sites(aggData_siteIDs,
                               datasettype = "diatom",
                                  all_data = TRUE) %>% 
  get_datasets() %>%
  neotoma2::filter(datasetid %in% aggData_df$`Neotoma Diatom Dataset Id`) %>%
  get_downloads(all_data = TRUE)

saveRDS(aggData_waterChem_dl,
        file = paste0(local_fp,
                      "Neotoma_Local/aggData_WaterChem.rds",
                      sep = ""))

saveRDS(aggData_diatom_dl,
        file = paste0(local_fp,
                      "Neotoma_Local/aggData_DiatomSamples.rds",
                      sep = ""))

```

#### Code: load data
```{r load_AD_loadData, eval = FALSE}
aggData_waterChem_dl <- readRDS(file = paste0(local_fp,
                      "Neotoma_Local/aggData_WaterChem.rds",
                      sep = ""))

aggData_diatom_dl <- readRDS(file = paste0(local_fp,
                      "Neotoma_Local/aggData_DiatomSamples.rds",
                      sep = ""))

# pull samples data for water chem and diatom strat samples
aggData_samples_waterChem <- samples(aggData_waterChem_dl)
aggData_samples_diatom <- samples(aggData_diatom_dl)

# pull taxa data
aggData_diatom_tx <- taxa(aggData_diatom_dl)
aggData_waterChem_tx <- taxa(aggData_waterChem_dl)

# Calculate each taxon's proportion within its sample,
# then keep the samples where taxas' proportion is above 10%
common_taxon <- aggData_samples_diatom %>%
  filter(units == "NISP") %>%
  group_by(sampleid) %>%
  mutate(proportion = value / sum(value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(proportion > 0.10)

# extract the twelve taxa that are most prevalent across the set
# need to refine how I calculate this
top_taxon <- common_taxon %>%
  group_by(variablename) %>%
  mutate(tot_taxa = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(tot_prop = value / tot_taxa) %>%
  mutate(rank = dense_rank(desc(tot_taxa))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
 filter(rank <= 25)

# pull out pH data from water chem
# drop observations with a pH > 14
waterchem_ph <- aggData_samples_waterChem %>%
  filter(variablename == "pH") %>%
  filter(value <= 14 & value >= 0)

# leaflet map
# set up palette
pal <- leaflet::colorBin("viridis",
                            domain = waterchem_ph$value)

map3 <- leaflet(waterchem_ph) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(lng = waterchem_ph$long,
                   lat = waterchem_ph$lat,
                   color = pal(waterchem_ph$value),
                   popup = paste0("<b>", waterchem_ph$sitename,
                                  "</b><br><a href=", 
                                  explorerURL, "?siteids=",
                                  waterchem_ph$siteid,
                                  ">Explorer Link</a>",
                                  "<br> <b>pH:</b>",
                                  waterchem_ph$value),
                   options = markerOptions(riseOnHover = TRUE)) %>%
  addLegend("bottomright",
            pal = pal,
            values = ~value,
            title = "pH",
            opacity = 1)

map3
```

### Using Aggregate Datasets: Merging data {.tabset}
Here, we'll join the diatom and water chemistry data we've extracted.We'll use `common_taxa` and `waterchem_ph` generated in the previous section.

We know that because we've pulled datasets for diatoms and water chemistry based on sites, we should be able to group data based on `siteid`. The field `taxongroup` in the generated output dataframe will identify which records are for water chemistry, and which are diatom data. We'll summarize our data by `siteid` and select or summarize only essential fields for the dataframe we're creating for our plot.

#### Code
```{r merge_diatom_waterchem, eval = FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=12}
# what are the variables in each dataframe?
colnames(waterchem_ph)
colnames(common_taxon)

# quick peek at the data in each field
head(waterchem_ph)
head(common_taxon)

# append datasets using `bind_rows`
diatom_waterchem_df <- bind_rows(list("diatom" = common_taxon,
                                      "waterchem" = waterchem_ph))

# create dataframe with top taxa and pH values, by siteID
taxa_to_join <- top_taxon %>%
  select(c("siteid","variablename","value","rank","tot_prop","sitename","lat","long","elev")) %>%
  group_by(siteid,sitename,lat,long,elev,variablename) %>%
  summarize(value_sum = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            rank = first(rank),
            tot_prop = first(tot_prop))

waterchem_to_join <- waterchem_ph %>%
  mutate(pH = value) %>%
  select(c("siteid","sitename","lat","long","elev","pH")) %>%
    group_by(siteid,sitename,lat,long,elev) %>%
    summarize(ph_mean = mean(pH, na.rm = TRUE))

taxa_ph_df <- left_join(taxa_to_join,waterchem_to_join,
                        by = c("siteid",
                        "sitename",
                        "lat",
                        "long",
                        "elev")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ph_mean))

# set up palette
pal2 <- colorBin("viridis",
                            domain = taxa_ph_df$ph_mean)

ggplot() + 
   annotation_map(
    map_data("world"),
    fill = "white", colour = "darkgrey"
  ) +
  geom_point(data = taxa_ph_df, mapping = aes(x = long, y = lat, size = value_sum, color = taxa_ph_df$ph_mean)) +
    scale_color_viridis_c("pH") +
  facet_wrap(~variablename,
             labeller = labeller(variablename = label_wrap_gen(width = 16)))+
   guides(color = guide_legend("pH"),
         size = guide_legend("Observations"))

```

```{r merge_diatom_waterchem_plot, echo = FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=12}
taxa_to_join <- top_taxon %>%
  select(c("siteid","variablename","value","rank","tot_prop","sitename","lat","long","elev")) %>%
  group_by(siteid,sitename,lat,long,elev,variablename) %>%
  summarize(value_sum = sum(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            rank = first(rank),
            tot_prop = first(tot_prop))

waterchem_to_join <- waterchem_ph %>%
  mutate(pH = value) %>%
  select(c("siteid","sitename","lat","long","elev","pH")) %>%
    group_by(siteid,sitename,lat,long,elev) %>%
    summarize(ph_mean = mean(pH, na.rm = TRUE))

taxa_ph_df <- left_join(taxa_to_join,waterchem_to_join,
                        by = c("siteid",
                        "sitename",
                        "lat",
                        "long",
                        "elev")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ph_mean))

# set up palette
pal2 <- colorBin("viridis",
                            domain = taxa_ph_df$ph_mean)

ggplot() + 
   annotation_map(
    map_data("world"),
    fill = "white", colour = "darkgrey"
  ) +
  geom_point(data = taxa_ph_df, mapping = aes(x = long, y = lat, size = value_sum, color = taxa_ph_df$ph_mean)) +
    scale_color_viridis_c("pH") +
  facet_wrap(~variablename,
             labeller = labeller(variablename = label_wrap_gen(width = 16)))+
   guides(color = guide_legend("pH"),
         size = guide_legend("Observations"))
```
### Leveraging Climate Data {.tabset}
Here we'll borrow some code from "A Simple Workflow" and adjust it to be more specific to work with diatoms. We'll pick a specific genus: Aulacoseira, and conduct an initial visual inspection for a relationship between its prevalence and minimum and maximum monthly temperatures.

This code is modified from a previous version of "A Simple Workflow:"

### 4.3. Distributions in Climate (July max temperature) from Rasters

We are often interested in the interaction between taxa and climate, assuming that time is a proxy for changing environments. The development of large-scale global datasets for climate has made it relatively straightforward to access data from the cloud in raster format.  R provides a number of tools (in the `sf` and `raster` packages) for managing spatial data, and providing support for spatial analysis of data.

The first step is taking our sample data and turning it into a spatial object using the `sf` package in R:

```{r makeSamplesSpatial}
modern <- aggData_samples_diatom %>% 
  filter(age < 1000) %>% 
  filter(ecologicalgroup == "DIAT" & elementtype == "valve" & units == "NISP")

spatial <- sf::st_as_sf(modern, 
                        coords = c("long", "lat"),
                        crs = "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84")
```

The data is effectively the same, `sf` makes an object called `spatial` that is a `data.frame` with all the information from `samples()`, and a column (`geometry`) that contains the spatial data.

We can use the [`worldclim_global()` function](https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/geodata/html/worldclim.html) in the `geodata` package to get climate data from WorldClim (geodata also has many other types of global data available!). The operations that follow here can be applied to any sort of raster data, provided it is loaded into R as a `raster` object.

You can load several types of monthly average climate data from WorldClim:

| Variable | Description | Unit |
| -------- | ----------- |------|
| tmin | minimum temperature | °C |
| tmax | maximum temperature | °C |
| tavg | average temperature | °C |
| prec | total precipitation | mm |
| srad | incident solar radiation | kJ m-2 day-1 |
| wind | wind speed (2 m above the ground) | m s-1 |
| vapr | vapor pressure | kPa |


Here we pull in the raster data, at a 10 minute (spatial, not temporal) resolution for the $T_{max}$ and $T_{min}$, maximum and minimum monthly temperatures, respectively.  The raster itself has 12 layers, one for each month.  We'll use the `extract()` function to just get the maximum temperature for July, and the minimum temperature for February (roughly, the max in the hottest month and min in the coldest month).

```{r worldTmax}
#worldTmax <- raster::getData('worldclim', var = 'tmax', res = 10)
worldTmax <- worldclim_global(var = "tmax", res = 10, path = tempdir(), version="2.1")
worldTmin = worldclim_global(var = "tmin", res = 10, path = tempdir(), version="2.1")

spatial$tmax7 <- raster::extract(worldTmax, spatial)[,7]
spatial$tmin2 <- raster::extract(worldTmin, spatial)[,2]

```

This adds a column to the `data.frame` `spatial`, that contains the maximum July temperature and minimum January temperature for each taxon at each site (all taxa at a site will share the same value). We have `r length(unique(spatial$variablename))` distinct names for the taxa.  We're going to use `dplyr`'s `mutate()` function to extract just the genus:

```{r toGenus}
spatial2 <- spatial %>%
  mutate(variablename = stringr::str_replace(variablename, "[[:punct:]]", " ")) %>% 
  mutate(variablename = stringr::word(variablename, 1)) %>% 
  group_by(variablename, siteid, sitename) %>% 
  summarise(tmax7 = max(tmax7),
            tmin2 = min(tmin2),
            count_sum = sum(value),
            .groups = "keep") %>%
  mutate(trange = tmax7-tmin2) %>%
  group_by(variablename) %>% 
  filter(n() > 20)
```

#### 4.3.1. Taxa specific mapping
Let's take a look (and map) some data for a specific genus: Aulacoseira.
First, we'll plot it with ggplot2, and then with Leaflet.
```{r Aulacoseira_focus}
aul <- spatial2 %>%
  filter(variablename == "Aulacoseira")

head(aul)

aul2 <- aul %>%
  mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[,1],
         lat = sf::st_coordinates(geometry)[,2])

ggplot() + 
  annotation_map(
    map_data("world"),
    fill = "white", colour = "darkgrey"
  ) +
  geom_point(data = aul2, aes(x =lon,
                              y =lat,
                              size = count_sum,
                              color = tmax7))+
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "inferno", direction = -1) +
  guides(color = guide_legend("max temp"),
         size = guide_legend("Observations"))+
  labs(title = "Max Temperature")

ggplot() + 
  annotation_map(
    map_data("world"),
    fill = "white", colour = "darkgrey"
  ) +
  geom_point(data = aul2, aes(x =lon,
                              y =lat,
                              size = count_sum,
                              color = tmin2))+
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "mako") +
  guides(color = guide_legend("min temp"),
         size = guide_legend("Observations"))+
  labs(title = "Min Temperature")

```

```{r Aulacoseira_focus_leaflet}
# leaflet map
# set up palettes
pal_hot <- leaflet::colorBin("inferno",
                            domain = aul2$tmax7,
                            bins = 5,
                            reverse = TRUE)

pal_cold <- leaflet::colorBin("mako",
                            domain = aul2$tmin2,
                            bins = 5)

aul_tmax <- leaflet(aul2) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(lng = aul2$lon,
                   lat = aul2$lat,
                   radius = ~ scales::rescale(aul2$count_sum, to = c(5,30)),
                   color = pal_hot(aul2$tmax7),
                   popup = paste0("<b>", aul2$sitename,
                                  "</b><br><a href=", 
                                  explorerURL, "?siteids=",
                                  aul2$siteid,
                                  ">Explorer Link</a>",
                                  "<br> <b>Max temp: </b>",
                                  round(aul2$tmax7,2),
                                  "<br> <b>Min temp: </b>",
                                  round(aul2$tmin2,2),
                                  "<br><b>Observations: </b>",
                                  aul2$count_sum),
                   options = markerOptions(riseOnHover = TRUE)) %>%
  addLegend("bottomright",
            pal = pal_hot,
            values = ~tmax7,
            title = "Max Temperature in July",
            opacity = 1)

aul_tmin <- leaflet(aul2) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(lng = aul2$lon,
                   lat = aul2$lat,
                   radius = ~ scales::rescale(aul2$count_sum, to = c(5,30)),
                   color = pal_cold(aul2$tmin2),
                   popup = paste0("<b>", aul2$sitename,
                                  "</b><br><a href=", 
                                  explorerURL, "?siteids=",
                                  aul2$siteid,
                                  ">Explorer Link</a>",
                                  "<br> <b>Max temp: </b>",
                                  round(aul2$tmax7,2),
                                  "<br> <b>Min temp: </b>",
                                  round(aul2$tmin2,2),
                                  "<br><b>Observations: </b>",
                                  aul2$count_sum),
                   options = markerOptions(riseOnHover = TRUE)) %>%
  addLegend("bottomright",
            pal = pal_cold,
            values = ~tmin2,
            title = "Min Temperature in February",
            opacity = 1)

aul_tmax
aul_tmin

```
